Module 1

The working directory

Before we start

Every time you open R, it is standing in one folder on your computer, and only one. That folder is called the working directory, and it is where R looks for the file you ask for and where it saves anything you create. Almost every "cannot open file" a beginner meets is not a broken file at all, it is R looking in the wrong place. In this lecture you will learn the two commands that settle it: getwd() to ask where R is standing, and setwd() to move it to the folder holding your data. By the end you will be able to check where you are, move to the right folder, confirm the move worked, and write a path that behaves the same on Windows, Mac and Linux.

Five steps on the board, four reference boards to keep, a short recap, then ten situations to try yourself.

The lecture, step by step

Five steps, in order, with the board and the console beside each one.

1What is a working directory?

The tutor opens with the idea itself: the working directory is the folder your R session is using, and any file you open or save goes there unless you say otherwise. On the board, the green box marks the line that is your working directory.

2How to check the current working directory

He points at the command. getwd() takes nothing in the brackets, and the console beside him shows what it prints back: the folder R is standing in right now.

3How to set a new working directory

setwd with the full path in quotes. Notice the examples panel: a Windows path with forward slashes, a drive path, and a Linux or Mac path, all written the same way.

4Check again

The step people skip. Run getwd() a second time and read the printed line: it has changed, so you know the move worked before you try to read a file.

5Remember: R reads and saves here

The consequence, in one picture. Once you change the working directory, the files you open and the outputs you save are all in the new folder.

The reference posters

The same four boards, presented in class. Between them they answer almost every working directory question.

1Printing the current working directory

Five people, five different folders, and the same answer every time: getwd() with empty brackets. What changes is the line R prints back.

2Setting a new working directory

Ricky, Tobias, Oumar, Saffa and Beatrize each need to move somewhere different. Every example ends with getwd(), because setwd prints nothing when it works.

3Forward and back slashes in R

Two columns, one recommended and one not. Forward slashes work on Windows, Mac and Linux, so they are what your scripts should use. A back slash is an escape character in R, which is why the example on the right fails, and panel 3 is the reminder to check getwd() when a path still will not open.

4The three step cycle

Where am I, move me there, did I move correctly. The strip along the bottom of the board is the part worth memorising.

Recap before you try

Everything on the five posters comes down to two commands and one rule. Read this once, then do the ten scenarios below.

  • The working directory is the one folder your R session is using. Every file name you type is looked for there and nowhere else.
  • getwd() asks where that is. It takes nothing in the brackets.
  • setwd("path") moves R somewhere else. The path goes in quotes.
  • setwd prints nothing at all when it works, so run getwd() again to confirm.
  • Use a forward slash in every path. It works on Windows, Mac and Linux. A back slash is an escape character in R, so avoid it in your code.
1Step 1
getwd()
[1] "C:/Users/Mohamed/Documents"

Step one, always. Read the line R prints back: that is the folder you are standing in. If it is not where your data lives, nothing else will work.

2Step 2
setwd("C:/Users/Mohamed/Documents/r-training")
# nothing is printed

Step two. The full path in quotes, all the way down to the folder holding your data. The silence is success, not failure. An error would appear in red.

3Step 3
getwd()
[1] "C:/Users/Mohamed/Documents/r-training"

Step three, and the one people skip. Ask again. The printed line has changed, so you know the move worked before you try to read anything.

4Step 4
setwd("C:\Users\Mohamed\Documents") # fails: a back slash is an escape character setwd("C:/Users/Mohamed/Documents") # use this, on every machine setwd("C:\\Users\\Mohamed\\Documents") # doubling works too, but why
Error: '\U' used without hex digits in character string

The mistake everyone makes once. Windows shows back slashes and people paste them in. In R a back slash is an escape character, so the line fails. Turn them all round. Doubling them also works, but the forward slash is the habit to keep because it is the same on every machine.

Your turn: ten scenarios

Each one is a situation with a person and a folder. Write the line of R they need and press Check. The marking is exact: every bracket, quote and capital letter has to be right, just as R requires. Spacing is the only thing forgiven.

0 of 10 correct
1

Mohamed has just opened R and does not know which folder it is using. What command should he run?

One command, and nothing goes in the brackets.

2

Jaline runs that command and R prints [1] "C:/Users/Jaline/Documents". Her csv is in C:/Users/Jaline/Documents/Data. What command moves R there?

setwd, then the full path in quotes.

3

Shannon has run setwd and nothing at all was printed. She thinks it failed. What should she run to see whether it worked?

Silence means success, so ask R where it is now.

4

Saffa copied this path from Windows Explorer: C:\Users\Saffa\Desktop\Analysis. Write the setwd line that will actually work in R.

Turn every back slash into a forward slash.

5

Ousmane is in C:/Users/Ousmane/Downloads and needs to work in C:/Users/Ousmane/Documents/Malaria. Write the command.

It does not matter how far away the folder is: the command is the same.

6

Ricky types setwd(C:/Users/Ricky/Documents) and R says object 'C' not found. Write the line correctly.

A path is text, so it needs quotes around it.

7

Tobias is asked to prove to his supervisor which folder he worked in. What single command gives him the answer to paste into his email?

The same command he started with.

8

Musa is working on a Linux server, where his folder is /home/musa/r-training. Write the command to move there.

No C: on Linux, but the command does not change.

9

Beatrize wants to be sure before she starts and again after she moves. Write all three lines, in order, to move to C:/Users/Beatrize/Downloads/Reports.

Where am I, move me there, did I move correctly.

10

Oumar gets cannot change working directory from his setwd line. Before retyping the path, what command shows him the folder R is in now?

Start from where you are, then correct the path.
